title: What the Fire Doesn't Take
logline: After a death in a village, volunteers from the local funeral-aid society take over the practical work of the house and yard, so the family can sit with their loss.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The slowing that the year shows reaches its end: after a death, a village funeral-aid society takes over the practical work so a family can sit with its loss.

thread_out.thread: The body ends, so what carries on? Weeks after a funeral, a family opens the room of someone who is gone and faces what a half-finished life becomes.

requirements: A village funeral-aid society willing to be filmed carrying out its ordinary work
A grieving family giving full, explicit, ongoing consent
Sensitivity and flexibility in scheduling around an actual death, not a staged one

suggestions.name: A village funeral-aid society (marana adahara samithiya)
suggestions.why: Village funeral-aid societies are a widespread, well-documented institution across rural Sri Lanka; Uva is suggested for geographic variety within the group.
suggestions.verify: A specific society, family and willingness to be filmed are all unverified and cannot be arranged in advance of a real death.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts describe a body's end as a series of stoppings rather than a single switch. After death nothing in it is renewed from within, and only heat and cold keep working on it.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: මරණය එක් මොහොතකින් සිදුවන නිවී යාමක් නොව පිළිවෙළින් සිදුවන නැවතීම් පෙළක් බවත්, මරණයෙන් පසු ශරීරය ඇතුළතින් අලුත් නොවී උණුසුම හා සීතල පමණක් එයට බලපාන බවත් අභිධර්මය විස්තර කරයි.
lesson.the_teaching: At the end of a life, the texts say, the body's streams of matter stop in a fixed order. Matter from past action stops being produced shortly before the last moment of mind and its last batch ceases with it; mind-born and food-born matter go on until death and fade soon after, since no mind arises in the body any more and a body without the life faculty makes no food-born matter. Only temperature-born matter continues in the corpse, for a long time. This fits the texts' general account of matter, which looks unchanged only while the conditions that keep producing it stay the same.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film stays with the practical work that fills the hours after a death: white flags along the lane, borrowed chairs, tea made in bulk, the collection book passed around, neighbours cooking and arranging. Set against the family sitting apart, this busy care shows a body that can no longer keep itself going now being looked after by others, and the film leaves the viewer to feel that shift without explaining it.

key_terms.en: death-consciousness: the last mind-moment of a life
temperature-born matter; the only kind that continues in a corpse

lesson.caution: This is not a clinical definition of death or a medical timeline, and it offers no consoling 'we return to nature': the texts say only that the life-sustaining streams genuinely stop.
lesson.builds_on: The shared household showed a body slowing; this film arrives at the stopping itself, and at what is left when a body is no longer renewed from within.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
